notice: Synthetic severity fixtures. Every report is invented for this repository and describes no real-world event, vessel, unit, or organisation; place names are real only so the geography is plausible. Labels are author-assigned against the rubric in README.md, not expert-adjudicated. What a model trained on this file learns is that rubric as the author applied it.

rubric.CRITICAL: Mass casualties; use or credible threat of a nuclear, chemical, or biological weapon; a national state of emergency; destruction of critical national infrastructure; direct armed escalation between states.
rubric.HIGH: Deaths; a vessel or aircraft lost, seized with crew aboard, or seriously damaged; hostages taken; a strategic route closed or blocked; compromise of an operational system at critical infrastructure.
rubric.MEDIUM: Injuries without deaths; property or cargo damage; detentions, seizures, or impoundments without harm to persons; temporary disruption to movement or service; protests involving clashes; sanctions imposed or tightened.
rubric.LOW: No casualties and no damage. Routine deployments, exercises, transits, patrols, statements, and monitoring reports. Attempts that failed without consequence.

cases.title: Frigate completes scheduled Red Sea patrol
cases.content: A frigate assigned to a multinational escort task group completed a scheduled patrol in the southern Red Sea on Thursday. No vessels were challenged and no engagement took place. The deployment was described by the task group as routine.

cases.title: Armoured column observed moving to exercise area
cases.content: An armoured column was observed travelling north-east toward a designated training area on Tuesday morning. The movement had been notified in advance under an existing transparency arrangement. No unusual activity accompanied it.

cases.title: Several hundred gather outside ministry building
cases.content: Between four and six hundred people gathered outside a government ministry on Saturday afternoon to object to a proposed fuel levy. The gathering dispersed by early evening. Police reported no arrests and no damage.

cases.title: Bulk carrier reports minor steering fault, continues passage
cases.content: A bulk carrier transiting the Singapore Strait reported an intermittent steering fault on Monday. Engineers restored full control within the hour and the vessel continued under its own power. No assistance was requested.

cases.title: Approach by two skiffs broken off before boarding
cases.content: The master of a container ship reported two skiffs closing on the vessel south of the Gulf of Aden on Sunday night. The master increased speed and activated the water curtain, and the skiffs broke off the approach. Nobody was hurt and the vessel was not boarded.

cases.title: Phishing campaign blocked at mail gateway
cases.content: A regional utility said a credential-harvesting campaign directed at its staff was blocked at the mail gateway over the weekend. No messages reached user inboxes and no accounts were compromised. The utility said its operational network was never exposed.

cases.title: Review of existing export list concludes without change
cases.content: A periodic review of an existing dual-use export control list concluded this week with no entries added or removed. Officials said the list remains under standing review. No new restrictions take effect.

cases.title: Thermal anomaly detected over remote grassland
cases.content: A satellite pass recorded a low-confidence thermal anomaly over sparsely populated grassland on Wednesday. Ground verification is not available. Detections of this kind are frequently agricultural burning.

cases.title: Ceasefire holds through third consecutive week
cases.content: Monitors reported that a local ceasefire arrangement held through a third consecutive week with no violations recorded. Both parties maintained positions without movement. Liaison meetings continued as scheduled.

cases.title: Two warships pass at close quarters without incident
cases.content: Two warships operating in the eastern Mediterranean passed within visual range on Friday. Bridge-to-bridge communication was established and both vessels held course. Neither navy described the encounter as unsafe.

cases.title: Suspect device found to be inert
cases.content: A suspicious package left at a transport interchange prompted a two-hour closure on Thursday. Disposal officers examined the item and determined it was inert. The interchange reopened and no injuries were reported.

cases.title: Joint exercise concludes on schedule
cases.content: A ten-day combined exercise involving units from three participating states concluded on schedule. Organisers said all phases were completed without incident. Participating units have begun returning to home stations.

cases.title: Sit-in at port entrance ends after talks
cases.content: A sit-in blocking a secondary port entrance ended on Wednesday after operators agreed to further talks with the union. Traffic resumed within two hours. No injuries or damage were reported.

cases.title: Fishing vessel recovered after engine failure
cases.content: A fishing vessel that lost propulsion twelve nautical miles offshore was taken under tow by a coastguard cutter on Saturday. All six crew were accounted for and in good health. The vessel was returned to harbour.

cases.title: Ministry issues routine advisory on border formalities
cases.content: A foreign ministry issued a routine advisory reminding travellers of unchanged documentation requirements at a land crossing. The advisory noted no change in conditions. No restrictions were announced.

cases.title: Scanning activity reported against public web estate
cases.content: A national computer emergency response team reported elevated scanning activity directed at publicly reachable web services. No successful intrusions have been attributed to the activity. Operators were advised to review exposed services.

cases.title: Escort convoy completes transit of high-risk area
cases.content: A convoy of four merchant vessels under naval escort completed a transit of a designated high-risk area on Monday without challenge. The escort has returned to its patrol box. No approaches were recorded during the transit.

cases.title: Tremor recorded offshore, no damage reported
cases.content: A tremor was recorded offshore early on Sunday. Authorities reported no damage on land and issued no wave advisory. Seismic monitoring continues as normal.

cases.title: Suspicious approach reported, vessel unharmed
cases.content: A product tanker reported a small craft approaching to within half a nautical mile before turning away, off the Gulf of Guinea, on Tuesday. The vessel maintained speed and was not boarded. No damage or injuries occurred.

cases.title: Air policing intercept conducted in accordance with procedure
cases.content: Fighters conducted a visual identification of an unresponsive aircraft near international airspace boundaries on Thursday. The intercept was carried out in accordance with published procedure and the aircraft continued on its flight plan. No protest was lodged.

cases.title: Licensing guidance clarified for humanitarian shipments
cases.content: Regulators published clarified licensing guidance intended to reduce delays to humanitarian shipments. The guidance restates existing exemptions and adds no new prohibitions. It takes effect immediately.

cases.title: Patrol reports quiet night along contact line
cases.content: A monitoring patrol reported a quiet night along a contested contact line with no small-arms fire recorded. Positions were unchanged at first light. The mission described conditions as stable.

cases.title: March passes without disorder
cases.content: A permitted march of an estimated two thousand people passed through the city centre on Sunday and dispersed at the agreed point. Organisers and police both described the event as orderly. No arrests were made.

cases.title: Container lost overboard in heavy swell
cases.content: A feeder vessel reported a single empty container lost overboard in heavy swell on Friday. The vessel was undamaged and continued to its next port. A navigational warning was issued for the drifting container.

cases.title: Delegations meet for scheduled maritime boundary talks
cases.content: Delegations met for a scheduled round of maritime boundary talks on Wednesday. Both sides characterised the session as technical. A further round was agreed for next quarter.

cases.title: Defaced page restored within the hour
cases.content: A municipal information page was defaced with political slogans early on Saturday and restored within the hour. The site holds no personal data and is separate from service systems. No further access was detected.

cases.title: Survey ship shadowed during transit
cases.content: A civilian survey vessel reported being shadowed at distance by a naval auxiliary during a three-day transit. No communication was attempted and no manoeuvres were assessed as unsafe. The survey continued on schedule.

cases.title: Group claims responsibility for leaflet campaign
cases.content: A proscribed group claimed responsibility for distributing leaflets in two districts overnight. No devices were found and no threats were assessed as actionable. Police increased patrols as a precaution.

cases.title: Wildfire contained within firebreak
cases.content: A wildfire that began on scrubland Tuesday afternoon was contained within an existing firebreak by nightfall. No structures were threatened and no evacuations were ordered. Crews remained on site overnight.

cases.title: Naval auxiliary makes routine port call
cases.content: A naval auxiliary made a routine three-day port call for replenishment on Monday. The visit was publicised in advance. No change to the vessel's assigned deployment was announced.

cases.title: Exchange of detainees completed under existing arrangement
cases.content: An exchange of detainees was completed on Saturday under an existing arrangement facilitated by an intermediary. All those transferred were reported in good health. Both parties confirmed the exchange was concluded.

cases.title: Reported sighting turns out to be fishing activity
cases.content: A reported sighting of armed craft in a high-risk area on Thursday was assessed after investigation to have been local fishing activity. No vessels were approached. The report was closed without further action.

cases.title: Agency publishes quarterly shipping volume figures
cases.content: A transport agency published quarterly figures showing shipping volumes broadly unchanged on the previous quarter. The agency noted no disruption to scheduled services. No advisories accompanied the release.

cases.title: Student demonstration ends peacefully
cases.content: A student demonstration over tuition changes assembled outside a university administration building on Thursday and ended peacefully after three hours. Administrators agreed to meet representatives next week. No incidents were reported.

cases.title: Grounding avoided after pilot intervention
cases.content: A laden bulk carrier came within a cable of a charted shoal on approach before a pilot ordered a course correction. No contact occurred and the vessel berthed normally. The port authority has opened a routine review.

cases.title: Outage traced to configuration error, not intrusion
cases.content: A four-hour outage at a regional booking platform was traced to a configuration change rather than to any intrusion. No evidence of unauthorised access was found. Service was fully restored by evening.

cases.title: Two entities removed from designation list
cases.content: Two entities were removed from a designation list following a successful delisting petition. Restrictions on the remaining listed entities are unchanged. The removals take effect immediately.

cases.title: Submarine surfaces for routine communications
cases.content: A submarine surfaced briefly in international waters for routine communications on Wednesday before submerging again. The activity was observed by a maritime patrol aircraft. Neither state commented further.

cases.title: Flood warning lifted as river levels fall
cases.content: A precautionary flood warning covering low-lying farmland was lifted on Friday as river levels fell. No properties were affected and no roads were closed. Monitoring continues through the season.

cases.title: Rotation of peacekeeping contingent completed
cases.content: The rotation of a peacekeeping contingent was completed over five days without incident. Incoming personnel have assumed duties at all sites. The mission reported no change to its posture.

cases.title: Armed men board tanker and take stores
cases.content: Armed men boarded a product tanker at anchorage overnight and removed ship's stores and crew valuables before leaving. The crew were mustered in the citadel and none were harmed. The vessel remains operational.

cases.title: Collision in fog damages both vessels
cases.content: Two coasters collided in dense fog in an approach channel on Tuesday morning. Both sustained hull damage above the waterline and neither is taking on water. No injuries were reported and both proceeded to berth under escort.

cases.title: Clashes at refinery gates leave several injured
cases.content: Clashes broke out between demonstrators and security personnel at the gates of a refinery on Wednesday. Local medics treated at least nine people for minor injuries. Production was unaffected and the gates reopened that evening.

cases.title: Ransomware halts administrative systems at port operator
cases.content: A port operator said ransomware encrypted administrative file servers on Sunday, forcing manual processing of documentation. Vessel movements and terminal operations were unaffected. The operator is restoring from backups and has notified regulators.

cases.title: New designations target shipping intermediaries
cases.content: Authorities designated eleven shipping intermediaries and four vessels said to be involved in evading existing restrictions. The designations freeze assets within jurisdiction and prohibit dealings. Affected operators have thirty days to wind down.

cases.title: Shelling damages buildings in border village
cases.content: Shelling on Monday night damaged four buildings including a school in a border village. Residents had already left the area and no casualties were reported. Both sides accused the other of initiating the exchange.

cases.title: Border closed to freight after troop build-up
cases.content: Freight traffic at a land crossing was suspended on Thursday following a build-up of forces on one side of the border. Passenger traffic continues under restrictions. Hauliers report queues of several hours.

cases.title: Coastguard detains trawler in disputed waters
cases.content: A coastguard cutter detained a trawler and its eight crew in disputed waters on Friday, escorting the vessel to port. The flag state has requested consular access. No injuries occurred during the boarding.

cases.title: Flooding closes coastal road and displaces families
cases.content: Two days of heavy rain closed a coastal road and forced around sixty families into temporary accommodation. No injuries have been reported. Authorities expect the road to reopen once debris is cleared.

cases.title: Device detonates outside empty office overnight
cases.content: A small improvised device detonated outside an empty commercial office shortly after midnight, breaking windows and damaging the facade. Nobody was present and no injuries were reported. An investigation is under way.

cases.title: Engine room fire extinguished, vessel under tow
cases.content: A fire in the engine room of a general cargo ship was extinguished by the crew within forty minutes on Sunday. The vessel lost propulsion and is under tow to a repair berth. Two crew were treated for smoke inhalation and released.

cases.title: Crew confined during two-hour boarding
cases.content: Boarders held eleven crew in the ship's mess for roughly two hours before departing with equipment and cash. No weapons were discharged and no crew were injured. The vessel resumed passage under naval escort.

cases.title: Blockade halts rail freight for a second day
cases.content: A blockade of a freight rail line entered a second day on Tuesday, halting scheduled ore shipments. Operators estimate several days of backlog once the line reopens. No confrontations have been reported at the site.

cases.title: Customer records exposed by misconfigured storage
cases.content: A logistics firm confirmed that a misconfigured storage bucket exposed customer contact records for an unknown period. The firm said no payment data was held in the affected store. Regulators have been notified and the store has been secured.

cases.title: Ceasefire violations recorded for a third day
cases.content: Monitors recorded small-arms exchanges along a contact line for a third consecutive day. Damage was reported to two unoccupied structures. No casualties have been confirmed by either party.

cases.title: Export licences suspended for named machine-tool firms
cases.content: Export licences for three named machine-tool manufacturers were suspended pending a compliance review. Shipments already in transit may complete. The firms said they are cooperating with the review.

cases.title: Unsafe manoeuvre forces destroyer to alter course
cases.content: A destroyer altered course sharply to avoid a closing vessel during a freedom of navigation transit on Thursday. No contact occurred and no damage was sustained. Both states have issued conflicting accounts of the encounter.

cases.title: Airspace restrictions imposed at short notice
cases.content: Airspace over a coastal area was restricted at short notice for announced live-fire training, forcing rerouting of commercial flights. Several departures were delayed by up to two hours. The restriction is scheduled to lift Friday.

cases.title: Landslide blocks highway serving inland terminal
cases.content: A landslide following sustained rain blocked the highway serving an inland container terminal on Monday. No vehicles were caught in the slide. Clearance is expected to take four days, with freight diverted to a longer route.

cases.title: Fuel terminal suspends loading after leak
cases.content: A fuel terminal suspended loading operations after a leak was detected in a transfer line on Wednesday. The leak was contained within the bund and no product reached the water. Loading is expected to resume within 48 hours.

cases.title: Attempted hijack repelled by armed security team
cases.content: An embarked armed security team exchanged fire with approaching craft off a West African coast on Saturday, and the craft withdrew. No injuries were sustained aboard the merchant vessel, which was not boarded. Minor superstructure damage was reported.

cases.title: Vessel impounded over documentation dispute
cases.content: Port authorities impounded a general cargo vessel on Friday pending resolution of a documentation dispute. The crew remain aboard and are being supplied. The operator expects release within a week.

cases.title: Tear gas used to disperse crowd outside embassy
cases.content: Security forces used tear gas to disperse a crowd that gathered outside an embassy compound on Sunday evening. Eleven people were treated for the effects of the gas and four were detained. The compound was not breached.

cases.title: Denial-of-service disrupts government portals
cases.content: A distributed denial-of-service attack made several government information portals intermittently unreachable for around six hours. No service-delivery systems were affected and no data was accessed. Mitigation is in place.

cases.title: Arson attack damages transmission equipment
cases.content: An arson attack damaged equipment at an unmanned transmission site overnight, interrupting coverage for part of a rural district. Nobody was present at the site. Engineers restored partial service within a day.

cases.title: Drone strike destroys unoccupied vehicle depot
cases.content: A drone strike destroyed an unoccupied vehicle depot in the early hours of Tuesday. No personnel were present at the time and no casualties were reported. The strike was the third in the area this month.

cases.title: Cable-laying vessel ordered out of survey area
cases.content: A cable-laying vessel was ordered to leave a survey area by patrol craft on Wednesday and complied. Work was suspended for the day and no damage occurred. The operator has asked its flag state to raise the matter.

cases.title: Reservists called up in border districts
cases.content: A partial call-up of reservists was announced in three border districts on Monday. Officials described the measure as precautionary and of limited duration. No change to the movement of civilians was announced.

cases.title: Port operator restricted from receiving listed cargo
cases.content: A port operator was prohibited from handling cargo consigned to newly listed entities. The operator said two scheduled calls will be refused. Existing contracts are under legal review.

cases.title: Wildfire forces precautionary evacuation of two hamlets
cases.content: A wildfire advancing on two hamlets prompted the precautionary evacuation of around two hundred residents on Thursday. No injuries were reported and no homes have been lost. Crews expect containment within two days.

cases.title: Anchor drag damages subsea cable
cases.content: A subsea telecommunications cable was damaged on Sunday by what operators assess was a dragging anchor. Traffic was rerouted and no outage was observed by end users. A repair ship has been chartered.

cases.title: Farmers block approaches to two border crossings
cases.content: Farmers blocked approaches to two border crossings with tractors on Tuesday, causing long queues for freight. Police did not intervene and no confrontations occurred. Organisers said the blockade will continue for a further day.

cases.title: Intrusion detected in corporate network of rail operator
cases.content: A rail operator detected an intrusion in its corporate network and isolated affected segments. Signalling and control systems are on a separate network and were not affected. Timetables ran normally throughout.

cases.title: Airport closes one runway after equipment failure
cases.content: An airport closed one of two runways on Friday after a lighting system failure. Departures were delayed by an average of forty minutes. The runway is expected to reopen once repairs are certified.

cases.title: Skiffs fire on tanker, no casualties
cases.content: Small arms were fired at a tanker from two skiffs in the southern Red Sea on Wednesday, striking the accommodation block. No crew were injured and the vessel continued at speed. Naval forces responded to the distress call.

cases.title: Artillery exchange reported across contested river
cases.content: An artillery exchange across a contested river was reported on Sunday evening, with impacts recorded on both banks. No casualties have been confirmed. Monitors described the exchange as the heaviest in six weeks.

cases.title: Explosive device disabled near pipeline valve station
cases.content: An explosive device placed near a pipeline valve station was located and disabled on Monday before detonation. Flow was suspended for six hours as a precaution and has since resumed. No injuries occurred.

cases.title: Laser directed at patrol aircraft cockpit
cases.content: A maritime patrol aircraft reported a laser directed at its cockpit from a surface vessel during a routine flight. The crew completed the sortie and reported no lasting effects. A formal protest has been lodged.

cases.title: Insurers withdraw cover for listed trade routes
cases.content: Two insurers withdrew cover for cargoes moving on routes associated with newly listed entities. Brokers expect rates to rise on alternative routings. No vessels have been detained.

cases.title: Additional air defence deployed to coastal sites
cases.content: Additional air defence systems were deployed to two coastal sites over the weekend, according to imagery analysis. Officials did not comment on the deployment. No change to civil aviation routing was announced.

cases.title: Storm damage closes fishing harbour for repairs
cases.content: Storm damage to a breakwater closed a fishing harbour for repairs expected to last three weeks. The fleet has been relocated to a neighbouring port. No vessels were lost and no injuries were reported.

cases.title: Water treatment works taken offline after contamination alert
cases.content: A water treatment works was taken offline on Thursday following a contamination alert. Supply was maintained from an alternative source and a boil notice was not issued. Testing is expected to conclude within days.

cases.title: Explosion damages tanker hull, two crew injured
cases.content: An explosion tore a hole in the hull of a product tanker in the Gulf of Aden on Wednesday morning. Two crew members were injured and the vessel is taking on water. It is under escort to a nearby port of refuge.

cases.title: Vessel hijacked with twenty-two crew aboard
cases.content: Armed boarders seized control of a chemical tanker overnight and the vessel is now steering toward the coast with twenty-two crew aboard. Contact with the master was lost after the first distress message. Naval forces are tracking the vessel.

cases.title: Airstrike on market kills at least nine
cases.content: An airstrike on a market district killed at least nine people and injured more than thirty, according to medical staff at two hospitals. Rescue work continued into the night. Responsibility for the strike has not been established.

cases.title: Suicide bombing at checkpoint kills six
cases.content: A suicide bombing at a security checkpoint killed six people, including four personnel, and wounded fourteen others. The area was sealed off and casualties were taken to a district hospital. A group later claimed responsibility.

cases.title: Missile strike disables merchant vessel
cases.content: A merchant vessel was struck by a missile in the southern Red Sea, disabling its steering gear and starting a fire in a cargo hold. The crew abandoned ship and were recovered by a warship. One crew member remains in a critical condition.

cases.title: Intrusion reaches control systems at electricity substation
cases.content: An intrusion reached operational control systems at an electricity substation, and operators reverted to manual control to maintain supply. No outage occurred but investigators confirmed the attackers had the ability to open breakers. A national response has been activated.

cases.title: Earthquake collapses buildings, casualties reported
cases.content: A strong earthquake collapsed a number of buildings in a provincial town early on Friday. Local officials reported at least twelve dead and dozens trapped, with search teams working through the rubble. Power and water supplies have been interrupted.

cases.title: Strait closed to commercial traffic during exercise
cases.content: Authorities closed a major strait to commercial traffic for seventy-two hours to conduct live-fire exercises. Dozens of vessels are holding at anchorages and operators are assessing diversions. Charterers warned of significant delay across the route.

cases.title: Ferry capsizes, several unaccounted for
cases.content: A passenger ferry capsized in worsening weather on Sunday afternoon. Rescuers recovered most of those aboard but several remain unaccounted for and three are confirmed dead. A search continues with air support.

cases.title: Offensive takes district centre after heavy fighting
cases.content: Forces took control of a district centre on Tuesday after two days of heavy fighting. Both sides reported significant casualties and civilians have fled toward neighbouring districts. Aid agencies have lost access to the area.

cases.title: Crew members taken ashore after boarding
cases.content: Boarders removed six crew members from a fishing support vessel and took them ashore, according to the operator. The remaining crew brought the vessel to a nearby port. Negotiations for the release of those taken are reported to be under way.

cases.title: Warships exchange fire in disputed waters
cases.content: Two warships exchanged fire in disputed waters on Thursday, with damage reported to at least one vessel and injuries among its crew. Both governments have summoned ambassadors. Naval movements in the area have increased sharply.

cases.title: Bombing of bus kills four, wounds nineteen
cases.content: A bomb detonated on a crowded bus during the morning commute, killing four passengers and wounding nineteen. Emergency services declared a major incident. Transport across the district was suspended for several hours.

cases.title: Ransomware halts hospital systems for two days
cases.content: Ransomware forced a hospital group to divert emergency admissions and cancel scheduled procedures for two days. Clinical systems remain offline and staff are working from paper records. The group has not said whether patient data was taken.

cases.title: Bulk carrier sinks after grounding, crew rescued
cases.content: A bulk carrier that grounded on a reef broke its back and sank in shallow water on Saturday. All twenty crew were rescued by helicopter, two with serious injuries. Salvors are assessing a significant fuel oil release.

cases.title: Cross-border strikes kill civilians in two villages
cases.content: Cross-border strikes overnight killed at least seven civilians in two villages and destroyed a dozen homes. Both governments have traded accusations. A previously agreed de-escalation mechanism has been suspended.

cases.title: Cyclone makes landfall, coastal districts evacuated
cases.content: A cyclone made landfall on Thursday night, destroying housing along the coast and cutting road access to three districts. Officials confirmed five deaths and said the toll is likely to rise. Around forty thousand people were evacuated in advance.

cases.title: Armoured divisions moved to forward positions
cases.content: Two armoured divisions were moved to forward positions along a contested frontier over the weekend, according to multiple imagery assessments. Diplomatic missions have advised nationals to leave the area. No exercise had been notified.

cases.title: Tanker seized and taken to anchorage under duress
cases.content: A tanker was seized and taken under duress to an anchorage, with its crew of eighteen held aboard. The flag state has demanded immediate release. Naval assets have been redirected to the area.

cases.title: Mine strike damages vessel in approach channel
cases.content: A vessel struck what investigators assess was a moored mine in an approach channel, flooding a forward compartment. Three crew were injured, one seriously. The channel has been closed pending clearance operations.

cases.title: Attackers disrupt fuel distribution scheduling system
cases.content: Attackers disrupted the scheduling system used to allocate fuel deliveries, forcing a distributor to suspend regional dispatch for thirty hours. Filling stations in two provinces ran dry. The distributor is restoring systems from offline backups.

cases.title: Shelling of residential district kills eleven
cases.content: Sustained shelling of a residential district killed eleven people and wounded more than forty, according to local authorities. Several apartment blocks were destroyed. Utilities to the district have been cut.

cases.title: Gunmen attack hotel, hostages taken
cases.content: Gunmen attacked a hotel used by foreign delegations on Monday evening and took an unknown number of hostages. Security forces surrounded the building and exchanges of fire continued for several hours. At least three people are confirmed dead.

cases.title: Fire in container stack burns for a second day
cases.content: A fire in a container stack aboard a boxship burned for a second day, with firefighting tugs alongside. One crew member died and four were injured in the initial response. The vessel is anchored offshore and salvors have boarded.

cases.title: Central bank assets frozen across major jurisdictions
cases.content: Coordinated measures froze central bank assets held across several major jurisdictions with immediate effect. Correspondent banking relationships were suspended the same day. Trade financing on affected routes has largely stopped.

cases.title: Dam overtops, downstream settlements flooded
cases.content: A dam overtopped after prolonged rain, flooding settlements downstream and forcing thousands from their homes. Four deaths have been confirmed and a number of people are missing. Engineers warn the structure remains under strain.

cases.title: Airspace closed as forces mass near frontier
cases.content: Civil airspace over a frontier region was closed indefinitely on Wednesday as forces massed on both sides. Carriers cancelled dozens of flights and rerouted transits. No date has been given for reopening.

cases.title: Drone boat strikes naval vessel at anchorage
cases.content: An uncrewed surface vessel struck a naval ship at anchorage, causing a hull breach and starting a fire. Two sailors were killed and several injured. The port has been closed to all movements.

cases.title: Ambush on convoy leaves eight dead
cases.content: An ambush on a supply convoy left eight dead and several vehicles destroyed on a highway east of the provincial capital. Reinforcements secured the site after several hours. The route has been closed to civilian traffic.

cases.title: Air traffic flow system degraded by intrusion
cases.content: An intrusion degraded a flow-management system used by an air navigation service provider, forcing manual separation procedures and heavy flight restrictions for eleven hours. Safety was maintained throughout but hundreds of flights were delayed or cancelled. A criminal investigation has opened.

cases.title: Master killed during attempted boarding
cases.content: The master of a general cargo vessel was killed by gunfire during an attempted boarding off the Gulf of Guinea. The crew repelled the attackers and the vessel made port under escort. The remaining crew were unhurt.

cases.title: Coordinated attacks on two police stations
cases.content: Coordinated attacks on two police stations in the early hours left five officers dead and a number of weapons taken. Reinforcements regained both sites by morning. A curfew has been imposed across the district.

cases.title: Missile barrage on capital kills dozens
cases.content: A sustained missile barrage struck residential and government districts of the capital overnight, killing dozens and wounding hundreds. Hospitals declared mass casualty procedures. The government has declared a state of emergency.

cases.title: Coordinated bombings at three sites kill more than forty
cases.content: Coordinated bombings at a transport hub, a market, and a place of worship killed more than forty people and wounded over two hundred. A national emergency was declared and all public gatherings were banned. Hospitals appealed for blood donations.

cases.title: States exchange direct strikes on military bases
cases.content: Two states exchanged direct strikes on each other's military bases for the first time, with casualties reported at multiple sites. Both have recalled ambassadors and moved forces to high readiness. Regional airspace has been closed.

cases.title: Earthquake devastates city, thousands feared dead
cases.content: A major earthquake devastated a city of two million overnight, collapsing housing across entire districts. Officials fear thousands are dead and a state of emergency has been declared nationwide. International search and rescue teams have been requested.

cases.title: Attack triggers cascading blackout across three regions
cases.content: A coordinated attack on grid control systems triggered a cascading blackout across three regions, cutting power to several million people for more than a day. Hospitals ran on generators and water pumping failed in places. A national state of emergency was declared.

cases.title: Chemical agent reported after strike on town
cases.content: Medical staff reported symptoms consistent with exposure to a chemical agent following a strike on a town, with dozens treated and several deaths. Investigators have been asked to deploy. The reports have been condemned by multiple governments.

cases.title: Attack on nuclear facility perimeter prompts alert
cases.content: Armed attackers breached the outer perimeter of a nuclear facility before being stopped short of the controlled area. The operator declared a site emergency and the regulator raised the national alert level. No release has been detected.

cases.title: Tsunami inundates coastline after offshore quake
cases.content: A tsunami generated by a large offshore earthquake inundated a stretch of coastline, destroying settlements and killing an unknown number of people. A national state of emergency is in force. Casualty figures are expected to rise substantially.

cases.title: Full mobilisation ordered as forces cross frontier
cases.content: A general mobilisation was ordered hours after forces crossed a frontier in strength at several points. Martial law has been declared and civilian movement restricted. Neighbouring states have begun emergency consultations.

cases.title: Strait blocked after tanker breaks up
cases.content: A laden tanker broke up in the narrowest part of a strategic strait, blocking the channel entirely and releasing a large volume of crude. All traffic has been suspended indefinitely and dozens of vessels are holding. Several crew are missing.

cases.title: Strikes on power grid leave millions without supply
cases.content: Successive strikes on generation and transmission infrastructure left several million people without power in freezing conditions. Deaths have been reported at hospitals affected by the loss of supply. Authorities described the situation as a humanitarian emergency.

cases.title: Warship sunk with heavy loss of life
cases.content: A warship sank after an attack in contested waters with heavy loss of life among its crew. Rescue operations recovered a number of survivors overnight. The state involved has declared a period of national mourning and warned of a response.

cases.title: Mass casualty attack at stadium
cases.content: An explosion at a packed stadium killed dozens and injured many hundreds in a crush that followed. Emergency services across the region were mobilised. The government declared three days of national mourning and a state of emergency.

cases.title: Water treatment controls manipulated at multiple plants
cases.content: Attackers manipulated dosing controls at several water treatment plants serving a metropolitan area, and operators detected the changes before supply was affected. A state of emergency was declared while the network was isolated and verified. Investigators described the intrusion as sustained and deliberate.

cases.title: Volcanic eruption forces mass evacuation
cases.content: A large explosive eruption forced the evacuation of more than a hundred thousand people and buried several villages in ash and debris. A national state of emergency was declared and regional airspace closed. Casualty numbers remain unclear.

cases.title: Nuclear-capable forces placed at heightened readiness
cases.content: Nuclear-capable forces were placed at heightened readiness following a sharp escalation, according to statements from the government concerned. Several states convened emergency sessions in response. Civil defence measures were announced in border regions.

cases.title: Passenger ship sinks with heavy loss of life
cases.content: A passenger ship carrying over five hundred people sank in deep water after a catastrophic flooding event. Rescuers recovered survivors through the night but the death toll is already in the dozens. A national day of mourning has been declared.

cases.title: Biological material reported stolen from laboratory
cases.content: Authorities confirmed that biological material was taken during a break-in at a research laboratory and has not been recovered. A national alert was issued and border checks tightened. Officials described the material as capable of causing mass harm if released.

cases.title: Capital falls after week of fighting, government flees
cases.content: The capital fell after a week of heavy fighting, with the government relocating and administrative control collapsing across the country. Casualty estimates run into the thousands. Foreign missions have suspended operations and evacuated staff.

cases.title: Flooding submerges province, emergency declared
cases.content: Record flooding submerged large parts of a province, displacing hundreds of thousands and cutting off entire districts. Dozens of deaths have been confirmed with many more feared. A national emergency has been declared and the army deployed.

cases.title: Blockade imposed on island, all shipping halted
cases.content: A blockade was imposed around an island territory, halting all commercial shipping and air links with immediate effect. Supplies on the island are reported sufficient for days rather than weeks. Several states have described the action as an act of war.

cases.title: Financial clearing system offline, emergency measures invoked
cases.content: The national clearing system was taken offline after a destructive attack corrupted core records, halting interbank settlement. Emergency liquidity measures were invoked and cash withdrawal limits imposed. Authorities said restoration would take days at minimum.

cases.title: Strike on displacement camp kills scores
cases.content: A strike on a camp sheltering displaced families killed scores of people, most of them civilians, according to aid organisations at the scene. Medical facilities in the area were overwhelmed. An independent investigation has been demanded.

cases.title: Carrier group and rival fleet in close confrontation
cases.content: A carrier group and a rival fleet manoeuvred in close confrontation for several hours, with weapons systems reported to have been trained and a collision narrowly avoided. Both states issued explicit warnings of force. Shipping has been advised to avoid the area entirely.

cases.title: Radiological device discovered in populated area
cases.content: A device containing radiological material was discovered in a densely populated area and made safe by specialist teams. A wide cordon was maintained for two days and residents were told to remain indoors. Officials said the device was capable of contaminating a city block.

cases.title: Gas carrier explosion devastates port district
cases.content: An explosion aboard a gas carrier alongside devastated a port district, destroying warehousing and damaging buildings over a wide area. Dozens are dead and hundreds injured, with people still unaccounted for. The port is closed indefinitely and a state of emergency declared.
